speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the room is spinning for you and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Did you notice any ringing in your ears, hearing loss, or a feeling of fullness in your ear during or after the episode? Also, did the spinning worsen when you moved your head?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the spinning lasted only three minutes and you feel back to baseline now; did the sensation stop completely if you kept your head perfectly still, or did it continue at a lower level? Also, have you ever had a history of ear infections, migraines, or recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms, I need to perform a bedside test to check if specific head movements trigger the spinning sensation. Let's try the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to see if we can reproduce your vertigo. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The Dix-Hallpike maneuver reproduced your symptoms, which strongly suggests a specific inner ear issue. To confirm, did you notice the nystagmus (eye jerking) stop after you sat back up, or did it continue? Also, has the spinning returned since you sat up from the test?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver combined with your lack of hearing loss or neurological symptoms points strongly toward Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo. I am confident in this assessment based on the clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
